# Lukoil (LUKOY) and Sberbank (SBRCY) Deep Dive Analysis

Report 044 | Published 2021-01-03 | Evaluated 2026-11-07

[Original member article](https://www.lynalden.com/premium-2021-1-3/) | [Article index](README.md) | [Structured review](../data/reviews/044.json)

Reflation, Bitcoin and Russian equities.

The dated Bitcoin view and the explicit 2021-22 cyclical catch-up call worked in declared proxies. The oil recovery view was stronger than the US production-peak scenario. Russian investor access remained the decisive weakness; valuation and low leverage did not offset it.

**Coverage:** All numbered text blocks and image labels read. Material theses, forecasts and explanations are included; routine holdings lists, incidental statistics, company descriptions and boilerplate are excluded. Chart pixels were not inspected.

## Claims

### 044-C01

**Fiscal money supports reflation**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Right |
| Type | forecast |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | US inflation |
| Source blocks | 13 |
| Thesis family | fiscal-monetary-reflation |

M2 kept rising and headline CPI reached 9.1% in June 2022. Direction is supported; the size of fiscal effects cannot be isolated from reopening, supply disruptions and energy shocks.

**Direction:** Resolved as stated.

**Timing:** No fixed endpoint supplied.

**Mechanism:** Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Outcome evidence:**

- [M2 monthly money stock](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/M2SL) | Federal Reserve via FRED | Verified in the audit

Latest vintage M2 rose from $19,375.3 billion in January 2021 to $19,874.5 billion in March and $20,457.7 billion in May.

- [June 2022 Consumer Price Index](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/cpi_07132022.htm) | Bureau of Labor Statistics | 2022-07-13 | Verified in the audit

June 2022 headline CPI rose 9.1% over twelve months.

### 044-C13

**Energy supply tightens after capex cuts**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Mixed |
| Type | forecast |
| Horizon | next few years |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | Oil |
| Source blocks | 94, 95, 108, 141 |
| Thesis family | oil-capex-supply-cycle |

EIA documented demand recovering faster than supply and WTI near $84 in November 2021. Later record US production shows that capital discipline was not a permanent production ceiling. The near-term tightness thesis worked better than the structural peak conjecture.

**Direction:** See reason; no return inferred.

**Timing:** Original horizon retained: next few years

**Mechanism:** Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Outcome evidence:**

- [Demand returns faster than supply](https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=50296) | EIA | 2021-11-09 | Verified in the audit

Demand largely recovered to 2019 levels in 2021 while October US production 11.4 mbpd remained below 2019 average 12.3. Inventories fell; WTI reached 84 on November 1.

- [More productive wells spur US crude production higher](https://www.eia.gov/todayinEnergy/detail.php?id=61523) | EIA | 2024-03-05 | Verified in the audit

US crude output averaged 13.3 million barrels/day in December 2023, exceeding the pre-pandemic monthly peak; greater well productivity supported record production despite declining drilling activity.

Russian law prohibited offshore depositary-receipt circulation. Lukoil announced ADR program termination effective December 30, 2022 and London listing cancellation June 6, with conversion arrangements for eligible holders.

- [U.S. Treasury escalates sanctions on Russia](https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/jy0705) | US Treasury | 2022-04-06 | Verified in the audit

Treasury imposed full blocking sanctions on Sberbank. The accompanying executive order prohibited new investment in Russia by US persons.

The three-to-five-year accessible-investment thesis failed for US ADR holders as blocking sanctions and program restrictions interrupted ordinary ownership and exit. This finding concerns the recommended instrument and audience, not a claim that the Russian bank became worthless. A holder-specific recovery ledger is still needed.

**Direction:** See reason; no return inferred.

**Timing:** Original horizon retained: three to five years

**Mechanism:** Business performance and shareholder return are distinct.

### 044-C31

**Cyclicals catch technology in 2021-22**

Across the named 2021-22 calendar period, financials, energy and industrial proxies all beat the Nasdaq-100 proxy: XLF +20.53%, XLE +151.88%, XLI +14.34%, QQQ -14.09%. Industrials lagged QQQ in 2021 alone, so the result is not a claim of continuous cyclical leadership. QQQ is a declared tech-heavy benchmark, not a pure technology index.

**Direction:** See independently checked outcomes and qualifications in reason.

**Timing:** Original horizon retained: 2021 and 2022

**Mechanism:** Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

## Framework lessons

- Separate jurisdiction from business quality.

## Verification limitations

- Retrieved 2026-11-07; publication-date wording is not authenticated.
- Public market series are available, but not every investment claim has a defined horizon or reconciled corporate-action-adjusted return. Unverified outcomes remain unscored; macro data use latest available vintages.
